title: A template's definition
description: What every templates/<name>/<name>.json says about its template: one of the app's real screens, or a few that link to each other, written as whole pages to copy and change. Its pages are beside it, in templates/<name>/.

name.description: What a designer calls it: the app's own name for the screen, such as Settings.

purpose.description: What it is, in a sentence or two.

when.description: When to start from it, each a kind of prototype, so someone choosing a template can match theirs.

screen.description: Which of the app's screens it is, in words, such as "Settings, the Settings tab, and the screens it opens".

screens.description: Its pages, in the order a journey meets them. The first is where it starts.

file.description: The page, beside the definition, such as index.html.

description.description: What the screen is, and how the journey gets to it.

components.description: The library's components its pages use, by element name. The build checks these are exactly the ones its pages use.

sources.description: The app's screens it was taken from. The same shape as a component's, but templates are iOS only for now, so only ios is needed.

notes.description: Anything else to know when changing it.
